audit.title: Data Streams Market Hours

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Sections open with liftable answers: "Cryptocurrency markets operate continuously. There is no designated market close and no `marketStatus` field." Minor weakness: the top intro leads with caveats ("depend on both…") before naming the canonical fact.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 16 sections, median 70 words, max 326, 0 over 600, 11 tables — ideal RAG chunk boundaries.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong. 158 numerals per 1k words, explicit UTC offsets, session times, holiday dates. The "0 with units" flag is a false alarm — times carry implicit ET/local units in context.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good. Links to NYSE and CME/NYMEX holiday calendars are authoritative primary sources despite the "0 primary sources" categorization; all schema references are internal.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. `marketStatus` value tables and the "Not mapped. Do not treat as Closed or Pre-market" Don'ts are crisp and liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Good but flawed. Valid TechArticle + BreadcrumbList, canonical present. Weaknesses: `dateModified` identical to `datePublished` (no revision signal), keywords are 23 comma-split tokens including stopwords, `about` entries are auto-template "Content about X" with a duplicate "Hours", and declared `programmingLanguage` lists TypeScript + Rust while the page has zero code.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak for the weight. Zero code fences. Acceptable for a lookup page, but a short snippet reading `marketStatus` from a report would help agents, and the schema's TS/Rust claim is unsupported.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good, concept-first. Covers setup → mapping → edge cases (early closures) but lacks symptom/error-phrased entry points.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Consistent naming of schemas (v8/v11), asset classes, and status values.

audit.summary: This is a dense, well-structured reference page mapping trading hours and `marketStatus` values across seven Chainlink Data Streams asset classes. Its biggest GEO strength is machine-scannability: 11 tables, clean H2/H3 hierarchy with zero level skips, and self-contained section leads that an engine can lift verbatim. The biggest opportunity is symptom-phrased query coverage — developers and agents will ask "what does marketStatus = 5 mean?" or "why is my equities feed returning 5?", and no heading matches that phrasing even though the answer sits in a table cell. Honest verdict: best-in-class reference content, retrieval-limited by concept-titled headings and a few auto-generated schema artifacts.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased lookup headings / FAQ
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "what does marketStatus 5 mean" or "why is my feed closed".
recommendations.change: Add H3s or an FAQ phrased as queries: "What does `marketStatus = 5` mean?", "Why does my US Equities feed return `2` or `5` only?", "What is `marketStatus = 1` for a v11 feed?" — each answered in one liftable sentence pointing to the right schema table.
recommendations.why: Devs query by value/symptom, not by "asset class overview"; concept-titled prose loses retrieval the FAQ phrasing wins.

recommendations.title: Lead intro with the canonical rule before caveats
recommendations.issue: "The correct `marketStatus` values depend on both the report schema version and the feed's trading-hours model."
recommendations.change: Prepend a one-line canonical map: "v8 (Forex/metals/commodities): 0/1/2. v11 standard-hours (US & APAC equities): 0/2/5. v11 24/5 equities: 0–5." Then the dependency sentence.
recommendations.why: Puts the highest-value fact in the first liftable sentence; defends against a skim answering from a single generic status table.

recommendations.title: Name the wrong-mapping Don't explicitly in the 24/5 vs standard section
recommendations.issue: The `1/3/4 = Not mapped` rows are correct but easy to miss when skimmed.
recommendations.change: Add a lead sentence: "For standard-hours v11 feeds, only `0`, `2`, and `5` occur — do not interpret `1`, `3`, or `4` as Pre-market/Post-market/Overnight; those apply only to 24/5 feeds."
recommendations.why: Prevents an engine from importing the 24/5 mapping (the tempting generic pattern) onto a standard-hours feed.

recommendations.title: Correct auto-generated schema metadata
recommendations.issue: Stopword-laden keywords, "Content about X" template `about` with duplicate "Hours", and `programmingLanguage: TypeScript, Rust` on a code-free page.
recommendations.change: Replace keywords with curated entity terms (marketStatus, RWA schema v8, RWA schema v11, NYSE hours, APAC equities); dedupe `about`; drop the TS/Rust `programmingLanguage` properties.
recommendations.why: Clean entity metadata aids entity resolution and trust; a false language claim undermines E-E-A-T signals to parsers.

recommendations.title: Emit a real `dateModified`
recommendations.issue: `dateModified` identical to `datePublished` — reads as generator-stamped, never revised.
recommendations.change: Wire `dateModified` to the actual last content edit and surface a visible "Last updated" line on-page.
recommendations.why: Visible freshness is an independent trust/recency signal for generative engines.

recommendations.title: Add a short marketStatus-read snippet
recommendations.issue: Zero code; agents get no runnable extraction example.
recommendations.change: Add a labeled 5–8 line snippet showing how to read the `marketStatus` field from a decoded v11 report and branch on `2`/`5`.
recommendations.why: Gives agents a copy-pasteable pattern and justifies the (currently unsupported) code-language schema claim.

antiPatterns: Auto-generated JSON-LD `keywords` split on commas into stopwords ("and", "for") and `about` template entries ("Content about hours") with a duplicate.
Declared `programmingLanguage` (TypeScript, Rust) with zero code on the page — schema/content mismatch.
No walls of prose, no unresolved cross-references, no ambiguous entities — clean otherwise.
offPageNotes: Consider listing this page in `llms.txt` and ensuring sibling pages (report-schema-v8, report-schema-v11, 24/5 US Equities User Guide) link back here as the canonical market-hours hub.
Freshness cadence: automate `dateModified` from the content pipeline rather than stamping publish time.
Third-party citation of `marketStatus` value tables is earned, not on-page controllable — the crisp tables help it happen.
